Predict exits from a survival model

predict.survival_model.Rd

  • Without newdata: the groups the model was fitted on (one row per tenure band, snapshot date and covariate values), with the exits expected next to the exits seen, to check how well the model fits.

  • With newdata: for each row, e.g. each person, the hazard of each exit type and the chance of retiring, leaving otherwise or staying within horizon years, e.g. for a simulation.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'survival_model'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, horizon = 1, ...)

Arguments

object

A survival_model from fit_survival_model().

newdata

NULL (the default), or a data frame with the panel's tenure column, covariates and, if the model has year effects, snapshot date column. A survival_panel works; a database table is collected.

horizon

Number. With newdata, the years ahead the chances are for, e.g. 1 / 12 for a month. Default 1.

...

Not used.

Value

A data.table.

Without newdata: the snapshot date, tenure_band (its lower bound), the covariates, exposure (years at risk) and, for each exit type modelled, exit_<type> (exits seen) and pred_<type> (exits expected).

With newdata: newdata plus hazard_<type> (exits per year at risk) for each exit type modelled and, if both were, prob_retired, prob_other and prob_stay, which add up to 1.

Details

Chances from hazards. The hazard is constant within a tenure band, so the chance of leaving within horizon is 1 - exp(-h * horizon), with h the sum of the two hazards, split between the exit types in proportion to their hazards. With one exit type not modelled, h is unknown, so no chances are given.

Levels with no exits. fixest drops a tenure band or year in which no one left (its fixed effect is minus infinity) and predicts NA there. The maximum likelihood estimate is 0 exits, so a band or year seen in the data but dropped gives 0; one never seen, or a covariate level never seen, gives NA.

No intervals. fixest gives no standard errors for its fixed effects, which carry most of a prediction, so none are given.

See also

fit_survival_model() for the model.

Examples

library(data.table)
contracts <- as.data.table(bra_hrmis_contract)
personnel <- as.data.table(bra_hrmis_personnel)
tenure <- compute_tenure_panel(contracts)
personnel <- merge(personnel, tenure, by = c("personnel_id", "ref_date"), all.x = TRUE)

panel <- build_survival_panel(
  personnel, contracts,
  tenure_col = "tenure_years", salary_col = "gross_salary_lcu",
  status_col = "employment_status", covariate_cols = "gender"
)
fit <- fit_survival_model(panel, band_width = 5)
#> Warning: 54 person-intervals have a missing value in `tenure_years` or `gender` and are left out of the model.

# exits seen and expected in each group
predict(fit)
